chapter.title: The power rule
text: To differentiate k xⁿ, bring the power down as a factor and lower the power by one: the derivative is k n xⁿ⁻¹. Then put in the value of x.

screens.title: In this order

modules.title: Integrate powers of x

chapter.title: Reverse the power rule
text: Differentiating xⁿ⁺¹ ⁄ (n + 1) gives xⁿ. So an antiderivative of k xⁿ is k xⁿ⁺¹ ⁄ (n + 1): raise the power by one, then divide by the new power.
math: ∫ k xⁿ dx = k xⁿ⁺¹ ⁄ (n + 1) + C

chapter.title: Between two limits
text: For a definite integral, work out the antiderivative F at the upper limit and at the lower limit, then subtract: F(upper) − F(lower). The constant C cancels.
math: Raise the power and divide: F(x) = 3x³ ⁄ 3

screens.title: Undo, then check
text: Whatever antiderivative you write, differentiate it: you must get back the function you started with. x³ differentiates to 3x², so ∫ 3x² dx = x³ + C.

screens.title: Two moves, then the limits
text: Add one to the power, then divide by that new power. Then put in the upper limit and the lower limit, and subtract.
math: Raise the power and divide: F(x) = 12x² ⁄ 2

screens.title: What the working needs
text: The working needs powers (2³ = 8) and fractions with the same denominator (16⁄3 − 2⁄3 = 14⁄3). If either is slow, practise it first; the integration itself is two moves.

modules.title: Integrate by substitution

chapter.title: Spot u and du
text: In ∫ 2x(x² + 1)² dx, call the inside of the bracket u = x² + 1. Its derivative, 2x, is already there: du = 2x dx. So the integral is ∫ u² du.

chapter.title: When doubling overtakes adding
text: Adding grows by the same amount each step (linear); doubling grows by more and more each step (exponential), so doubling always overtakes in the end.
math: Plan A: ₹42 on day 0, then ₹9 more each day. Plan B: ₹9 on day 0, then doubled each day. On which day is Plan B first worth more than Plan A?
chapter.tip: After n days of doubling the amount is ₹9 × 2ⁿ, not ₹9 × 2 × n: each day multiplies by 2 again.

screens.title: The method
text: Make a table of the two plans day by day: add for one, double for the other, and look for the first day the doubling plan is bigger.
